scope: Theorem 4.1 (Discretized planar Furstenberg estimate) of the manuscript “Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere” (preprints/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 077 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 669efdbef9150144), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 0 < k ≤ 2 and 0 < σ ≤ 1. For every ε > 0 there is η = η(ε, k, σ) > 0 such that the following holds for sufficiently small dyadic δ. Suppose P is a (δ, k, δ−η)-set of pins in a fixed bounded planar region, normalized to [0, 1]2. For every p ∈ P, let T (p) be a family of δ-tubes meeting p, with |T (p)| ≍ M, whose directions form a (δ, σ, δ−η)-set. Then [ p∈P T (p) ≳ε δ− min{k,(k+σ)/2,1}+ε M. Consequently the union has lower exponent at least min{k + σ, (k + 3σ)/2, 1 + σ} as the nonconcen- tration losses tend to zero.
